I have been working this land for 35 years. I know what it needs. My back is not what it was, and my son works in the city, so I need to keep things manageable. The wheat-maize rotation has fed my family all my life and I will keep it.

**Wheat (winter):** I plant the whole field — all 10.1 mu — in October after the maize comes off. I use the improved variety I have been buying from the county seed shop for years. It does not fail me. I apply base fertilizer when I till, then topdress urea at jointing. I water three times: once before winter freeze, once at jointing, once at heading. My well has never run dry. I spray for aphids and powdery mildew when I see them — two rounds usually. I do rotary tillage to chop up the maize stubble and work it in. I expect about 450 jin per mu, which is normal for my land.

**Maize (summer):** Right after wheat harvest in June, I get the maize in fast. I direct seed — no tilling — to save moisture and my knees. I buy hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or whatever the shop has that season, same as everyone around here. I apply compound fertilizer at planting and topdress nitrogen at the big bell stage when the plants are knee-high. Summer rains help but I water twice if it is dry — at establishment and at silking. I spray herbicide early and watch for corn borer. I expect around 550 jin per mu.
